name: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
venue: AAAI 2024 (Proceedings of the 38th AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, vol. 38 no. 17, pp. 19632-19642; Oral). Preprint arXiv:2308.10144 (cs.LG/cs.AI/cs.CL), submitted 20 Aug 2023, last revised 20 Dec 2024 (v3).
authors_affiliation: Andrew Zhao, Daniel Huang, Quentin Xu, Matthieu Lin, Yong-Jin Liu, Gao Huang (corresponding author). Tsinghua University (Department of Automation / Department of Computer Science, BNRist; LeapLab THU). Andrew Zhao and Gao Huang marked with one affiliation symbol; Daniel Huang, Quentin Xu, Matthieu Lin, Yong-Jin Liu with another; acknowledgement credits the Guoqiang Institute of Tsinghua University and NSFC grants.
task_domain: LLM-agent sequential decision-making / planning across knowledge-intensive QA (HotpotQA), embodied household tasks (ALFWorld), web interaction/shopping (WebShop), and fact verification (FEVER, transfer). Spans QA, embodied, and web/decision-making domains.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, gradient-free (no parameter updates) experiential learning. Two phases: (1) an offline TRAINING phase where the agent (a ReAct planner wrapped with Reflexion) autonomously gathers success/failure experiences via trial-and-error over a collection of training tasks, storing trajectories in an experience pool and distilling natural-language insights; (2) an EVALUATION phase where, on unseen tasks, the agent makes a single attempt (no retries) augmented with the extracted insights plus top-k retrieved similar successful trajectories. Deterministic, text-observation environments. Supervision is limited to a few manual fewshot demonstrations per environment (taken from ReAct/Reflexion); environment success/failure signals drive experience collection and insight extraction. A transfer-learning variant moves insights from a source domain (HotpotQA) to a target domain (FEVER) via insight 'finetuning' with a few target demos.
what_is_retrieved: (1) Successful past trajectories (full ReAct trajectories) from the agent's own experience pool, retrieved as semantically similar fewshot in-context demonstrations; and (2) extracted natural-language insights (cross-task guidelines/best-practices) which are not retrieved per-query but concatenated wholesale into the task specification. So retrieval proper targets self-generated successful experiences/trajectories; insights are abstracted experiences injected directly.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes itself: the experience pool is populated by the agent's own trial-and-error trajectories during the training phase (seeded with manual fewshot examples). It is a self-generated episodic store rather than a static external corpus. Note: the pool is grown offline during training and then frozen for the single-attempt evaluation phase, so growth is offline-induced, not test-time streaming.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: a fixed number k of most task-similar successful trajectories is retrieved (k set per environment, e.g. HotpotQA k=6, ALFWorld k=2, WebShop k=2, FEVER k=3). No completeness/minimal-set objective and no variable-size precision-driven recommendation; selection is fixed-k maximum-inner-product nearest-neighbor.
retrieval_unit: full trajectory: a complete successful ReAct trajectory (thought-action-observation sequence for a whole task) stored in the experience pool and retrieved as a fewshot exemplar. The complementary insight unit is a guideline-rule (natural-language insight), but that is injected directly rather than retrieved per-query.
index_source: Growing memory, offline-induced: the retrievable store (Faiss experience pool) is built from the agent's self-collected successful trajectories during the offline training phase (initialized with manual fewshot examples F_manual), then used during the single-attempt evaluation phase. Not a static external corpus; not online/test-time-grown during evaluation.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: a Faiss vectorstore of trajectory embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2) queried by kNN maximum-inner-product task similarity. No graph or hierarchical/cluster organization. Insights are kept as a separate flat list with importance counts (not a vector index).
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) kNN retriever: all-mpnet-base-v2 sentence embeddings over a Faiss vectorstore, ranked by maximum inner-product (task-description) similarity. Off-the-shelf, not learned.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf): the retriever uses a pretrained all-mpnet-base-v2 embedder with a fixed kNN/maximum-inner-product similarity over task descriptions; there is no contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback, RL, or downstream-task-effectiveness training of the retriever. (Insights, by contrast, evolve via LLM-driven ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE operations, but that is not retriever training.)
query_construction: Raw task input: the evaluation task specification/description is embedded and used as the query key to find maximum-inner-product similar successful training trajectories. No query decomposition, intent extraction, or synthetic expansion for retrieval. (Insights are not query-conditioned; the full insight list is concatenated.)
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): similar-trajectory retrieval is performed once per evaluation task at the start, conditioned on the task description; the retrieved fewshot exemplars are fixed for the whole episode. (The paper notes that in the reason-similarity ablation, retrieval could be done per-reasoning-step, but the default ExpeL uses task-level retrieval.)
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: retrieval of similar successful trajectories happens once at the beginning of each evaluation task and the result is used as fixed fewshot exemplars; the agent does a single attempt with no retries during deployment. Insights are likewise applied once (concatenated into the prompt).
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered unconditionally at the start of every evaluation task (top-k similar successful trajectories are fetched and inserted into the prompt). There is no confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier/reflection-token trigger; retrieval is not agent-initiated mid-episode in the default setup.
reranking: None. After kNN maximum-inner-product retrieval the top-k trajectories are used directly as fewshot examples; no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time: retrieved successful trajectories are injected verbatim as fewshot exemplars without compression, decomposition, distillation, or distractor filtering. (Separately, insights undergo an LLM-managed importance-count voting/EDIT process at write/extraction time, but that is abstraction of experiences into insights, not post-retrieval refinement of fetched trajectories.)
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: the evaluation prompt is the base ReAct prompt augmented by (1) the concatenated list of extracted natural-language insights appended to the task specification, and (2) the top-k dynamically-retrieved similar successful trajectories used as fewshot in-context demonstrations. No fine-tuning / latent injection; everything is in-context.
planning_integration: one-shot exemplars at plan time: ExpeL augments a base ReAct planning agent. At evaluation, insights + top-k similar successful trajectories are assembled once into the ReAct prompt, and the agent then runs ReAct (think-act-observe) for a single attempt. Retrieval is plan-/task-level (retrieve-then-plan); there is no per-step re-retrieval, no MCTS/tree search, and no hierarchical subtask decomposition in the default method.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (per-task/per-episode): retrieval and insight injection occur once per task before the ReAct rollout; the retrieved exemplars and insights remain fixed throughout the multi-step ReAct reasoning of that episode. Not per-CoT-step or per-tool-call (default).
retrieved_item_representation: Two surface forms: (a) raw successful ReAct trajectories (thought/action/observation text) injected as fewshot exemplars; and (b) distilled natural-language guidelines/insights (free-text rules such as 'consider the answer might be in the observations already made') concatenated into the task specification.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mixed: retrieved trajectories are raw full trajectories (concrete demonstrations), while the injected insights are distilled cross-task strategies/guidelines (high-level abstractions). The paper explicitly frames these as the two complementary human learning modes: storing/recalling specific successful trajectories vs. extracting high-level generalizable insights.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Insight-level robustness via an importance-count voting mechanism: each insight starts with importance count 2 and is incremented by UPVOTE/EDIT and decremented by DOWNVOTE, with insights removed at count zero, so that suboptimal/misleading insights (even from suboptimal successful trajectories) are pruned. Using gpt-4-0613 (vs gpt-3.5-turbo) for insight extraction reduces hallucination. Retrieval-side robustness comes from selecting maximum-task-similarity successes (ablation shows random sampling significantly hurts). The paper also found that adding raw reflections into insight extraction hurt performance due to hallucination, so reflections are excluded.
memory_type: episodic (experience pool of successful trajectories in a Faiss vectorstore) combined with a distilled natural-language insight/guideline store (a semantic/procedural-knowledge list). Primarily episodic-experience memory plus an abstracted-insight memory.
write_back: Yes. During the training phase the agent writes its trial-and-error trajectories into the experience pool B (all attempt trajectories are ingested; only successful ones are retrievable as demonstrations) and writes/edits cross-task insights into the insight list. No new entries are written during the single-attempt evaluation phase.
online_growth: No (not at deployment/test-time): the experience pool and insight list grow only during the offline training phase via trial-and-error; they are frozen for the single-attempt evaluation. The paper notes that for truly lifelong learning, extra retrieval over a growing insight set might be needed, framing test-time growth as future work.
write_back_trigger: on-success-and-failure (during training): the experience pool ingests every finished trajectory (both successes and failures) at each Reflexion trial; successful trajectories become retrievable demonstrations and success/failure pairs feed insight extraction. Insight writes are reflective/comparison-driven: the insight-extraction LLM ADDs/EDITs/UPVOTEs/DOWNVOTEs insights when shown fail/success pairs or lists of L successes. No writes during evaluation.
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure used, but differently: (1) for retrieval/demonstrations, only SUCCESSFUL trajectories are recalled; (2) for insight extraction, FAILED trajectories are explicitly contrasted with successful ones for the same task (success/failure pairs) to surface mistakes and best practices, so failures are leveraged to derive corrective guidelines rather than retrieved as exemplars. Reflexion reflections on failures drive re-attempts during training but are deliberately NOT fed into insight extraction (found to hurt).
memory_evolution_update: Insight store: link-and-evolve / refine via LLM operators ADD, EDIT, UPVOTE, DOWNVOTE with an importance count; insights are edited/merged/upvoted/downvoted and pruned (forget) when count hits zero, i.e. dynamic mutation beyond append-only. Experience pool: append-only (trajectories are added during training; no described merge/overwrite of stored trajectories).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Trajectory selection is fixed dense kNN top-k by maximum-inner-product task similarity using an off-the-shelf embedder; it is not an RL/value-optimized or learned retrieval policy. The agent is described as analogous to off-policy/experience-replay learning, but the selection rule itself is a fixed similarity heuristic.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory (one ExpeL agent's own experience pool and insights). The work does demonstrate cross-TASK and cross-DOMAIN transfer (HotpotQA->FEVER insight transfer) but not sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous agent frameworks.
benchmarks: HotpotQA (100 distractor dev-split validation tasks, Wikipedia Docstore API search), ALFWorld (134 solvable household tasks across 6 types: put, clean, heat, cool, look, puttwo), WebShop (100 tasks, online-shopping environment with reward score r in [0,1]), and FEVER (fact verification, used as transfer-learning target from HotpotQA). Same task subsets as ReAct/Reflexion; four-fold validation (train on one half, evaluate on the other and vice versa).
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (HotpotQA), fact-verification QA (FEVER), embodied (ALFWorld), web (WebShop).
baselines: ReAct and Act (Yao et al. 2023) as the main prompt-based planning agents (all use gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 at evaluation); Imitation Learning (IL) results taken from the ReAct paper (gradient-based); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) for the cross-task / task-reattempt comparisons (R0-R3); plus internal restricted variants ExpeL (insights-only) and ExpeL (retrieve-only). Transfer baselines: Act, ReAct, and ExpeL Transfer w/o Task Demos.
key_metrics: Success rate (%) - exact match for HotpotQA and FEVER, task completion within step budget for ALFWorld, purchasing item matching all attributes for WebShop; WebShop also reports mean reward score r in [0,1]; ALFWorld reports per-task-type success-rate breakdown. Auxiliary statistics: average thoughts/actions/observations, invalid actions, and token counts per trajectory.
headline_result: ExpeL consistently outperforms ReAct/Act across all three domains without parameter updates and without retries at evaluation: HotpotQA success rate ~39% (39.0 +/- 1.7), ALFWorld ~59% (59.0 +/- 0.3) success rate, and WebShop mean reward 0.701 (best across all agents; exact WebShop success-rate % is only shown in Fig.5 and not tabulated in text [uncertain]). It matches Reflexion on HotpotQA (39% vs 40% at R3) and outperforms it on ALFWorld (59% one-attempt vs 54.4% Reflexion R3) without repeated attempts, and shows positive forward transfer HotpotQA->FEVER (70% vs 63% ReAct).
ablations: (1) Learning-mode synergy (Fig.5/Tab.5): insights-only vs retrieve-only success rates are 36%/31% on HotpotQA and 50%/55% on ALFWorld (37%/38% SR and 0.675/0.67 reward on WebShop), with full ExpeL beating both, showing insight extraction and similarity retrieval are complementary and synergistic (insights dominate on HotpotQA, retrieval on ALFWorld). (2) Amount/diversity of experience (Fig.6): an agent extracting insights only from the initial fewshots has no advantage over ReAct; more autonomously-gathered experience helps, and Reflexion-gathered success/failure diversity beats ReAct-only gathering. (3) Insight-extraction ablations (Tab.3, HotpotQA): LLM-learned insights > hand-crafted insights > ReAct; adding raw reflections into insight extraction HURTS (hallucination); gpt-4-0613 insight extractor > gpt-3.5-turbo-0613. (4) Retrieval ranking (Tab.3, ALFWorld): task-similarity (ExpeL, 59.0) > reason-similarity > random sampling (significant drop), justifying task-similarity ranking. (5) Task reattempts (Tab.2): ExpeL+Reflexion improves with rounds (ALFWorld 59.0->64.2 over R0-R3) and beats ReAct+Reflexion at every round.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task success rates (and WebShop reward) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately, since retrieval here is trajectory recall for fewshot prompting rather than a ranked retrieval benchmark.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (success rate / reward). Some process-level statistics are reported in the appendix (average number of thoughts, actions, observations, invalid actions, and tokens per trajectory) and qualitative behavioral analyses (hypothesis formulation, world-model belief update, self-correction), but no formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reports token overhead vs accuracy in the appendix (Tab.6): ExpeL uses more tokens per trajectory than ReAct due to injected insights+exemplars (e.g. HotpotQA ~4310 vs ReAct ~1320 tokens; ALFWorld ~2857 vs ~2051; WebShop ~3291 vs ~2575), trading extra context tokens for higher success. Emphasized efficiency angles: no parameter updates / no GPU finetuning, no need for large human-labeled datasets, and a single evaluation attempt with no test-time retries (unlike Reflexion's repeated trials). No explicit dollar/latency figures given.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k, budget-capped: max fewshot examples k per environment - HotpotQA k=6, ALFWorld k=2, WebShop k=2, FEVER k=3 (plus k_reflections=2); number of success examples L per insight-extraction batch is 8 (HotpotQA, ALFWorld) or 4 (WebShop). The full extracted insight list is concatenated (kept under the LLM token limit; paper notes insight retrieval may be needed for lifelong settings). Selection is fixed-k retrieved-then-used (no adaptive/precision-driven k).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks: HotpotQA 100 distractor-dev tasks; ALFWorld 134 solvable tasks (6 types); WebShop 100 tasks; FEVER for transfer; four-fold validation, same subsets as ReAct/Reflexion).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (task-similarity kNN recall of successful trajectories), Reuse: yes (trajectories as fewshot exemplars; insights as guidelines), Revise: partial (insights are revised/edited via ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE during training, but retrieved trajectories themselves are reused verbatim and not adapted per-case at solve time), Retain: yes (writes successful trajectories to the experience pool and abstracted insights to the insight store during training)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as experiential learning / experience-replay / off-policy learning (citing Lin 1992, Watkins & Dayan 1992, Sutton & Barto) and does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term case-based reasoning; it realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under experiential-learning and RAG framing.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; the only tool is a fixed Wikipedia Docstore search API for HotpotQA/FEVER, not a retrievable tool index).
index_content_separation: N/A. No separation of a lightweight retrievable index from heavy on-demand content; full successful trajectories are both indexed (via embeddings) and loaded as exemplars; the full insight list is loaded wholesale.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; environment interaction via ReAct action APIs and a Wikipedia Docstore API, not MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful tool stores).
adaptation_mechanism: Mostly verbatim ICL exemplar reuse for retrieved trajectories (retrieved successful trajectories are injected as-is as fewshot demonstrations). The abstraction/adaptation happens at the insight level: an LLM extracts/edits cross-task insights via ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE from success/failure comparisons, providing LLM-prompted generalization rather than per-case solution adaptation. No execution-feedback case revision at solve time in the default single-attempt setting.
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023, base think-act-observe planning agent and fewshot prompts/templates) and Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023, used to gather diverse success/failure experiences via self-reflective retries during training); semantic-similarity in-context example selection (Liu et al. 2022 KATE-style); experience replay / off-policy RL framing (Lin 1992; Watkins & Dayan 1992; Sutton & Barto 2018); Faiss vectorstore (Johnson et al. 2019) and all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings (Song et al. 2020); RAG for decision-making (Humphreys et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: Finetuning-based LLM-agent learning (resource-heavy, needs parametric access, can hurt generalization); Reflexion (intra-task self-improvement via repeated retries on the SAME task, lacks cross-task memory) - ExpeL emphasizes inter-task/cross-task learning with a single evaluation attempt and no retries; standard RAG that retrieves gold/external examples - ExpeL instead retrieves its OWN self-generated experiences; imitation-learning baselines.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience planning): an experience/insight-memory LLM agent in the lineage of feedback-driven planning agents (ReAct -> Reflexion -> ExpeL), pioneering gradient-free cross-task experiential learning that retrieves self-generated successful trajectories plus distilled natural-language insights at inference. A canonical predecessor for later experience/case-based retrieval-augmented agents (e.g., trajectory-bootstrapping and guideline/insight-distillation methods).
